stories.title: Split I15 capability verdicts so one degraded capability cannot mask another
stories.description: verify-code-intel.mjs I15 must emit one verdict per declared capability instead of a single combined verdict, so an uncovered capability cannot suppress another capability fallback. Observed 2026-09-22: .gitnexus/gitnexus.json declares fts=unavailable (provider ladybugdb-fts, NO reason recorded) and vectorSearch=unavailable (provider exact-scan, reason "LadybugDB VECTOR is disabled on this platform; semantic search uses exact scan when embeddings exist"). The fallback branch is gated on bad.every(b => b.startsWith("vectorSearch")), so fts being down makes that test false and the vectorSearch fallback is never considered - even though .code-review-graph/graph.db (455MB) is present and is exactly the provider the fallback looks for. Accepted outcome: vectorSearch resolves via the code-review-graph witness; fts reports its own verdict and, having no provider, still fails. Do NOT force the run green - the file honesty rule is that a check it cannot stand behind reports unverified, never pass.
steps: Read scripts/verify-code-intel.mjs I15 and confirm the combined-verdict bug at the bad.every(...) guard.
Restructure I15 to record one result per capability key from gitnexus.json capabilities.
Apply the existing code-review-graph fallback per-capability rather than only when every failure is vectorSearch.
Record fts with its own verdict; note in the detail string that gitnexus.json supplies no reason for it.
Preserve the exit-code contract: any capability with no provider still yields exit 1.
Run node scripts/verify-code-intel.mjs and confirm separate per-capability lines and an honest exit code.

stories.title: Correct the declared codebase-memory-mcp tool count and gate it
stories.description: The declared codebase-memory-mcp tool count must equal the server actual count, and a check must fail when it does not. Observed 2026-09-22: the live server exposes 14 tools (delete_project, detect_changes, get_architecture, get_code_snippet, get_graph_schema, index_repository, index_status, ingest_traces, list_projects, manage_adr, query_graph, search_code, search_graph, trace_path) while four non-snapshot files claim 11: agents/graph-navigator.md:4, apps/prism-setup/resources/plugin/agents/graph-navigator.md:4, and .prism/shared/docs/code-intel/prism-code-intelligence-integration.md at :78 and :299. CLAUDE.md carries no count and needs no edit. The prism-setup copy is a propagation target, so correcting only the authored agent ships the wrong scaffold. A second drift rides along: the graph-navigator body calls the tool trace_call_path; the server actual tool is trace_path. Prefer wording that cannot go stale again over a hardcoded number.
steps: Correct the tool-count claim in all four non-snapshot locations; leave .prism/shared/evals/ snapshots untouched.
Correct trace_call_path to trace_path in the graph-navigator body.
Add a check that compares the declared count against the server actual tool list and fails on drift.
Verify with: grep -rn "11 tools" --include=*.md . | grep -v "/evals/"  returns nothing.
Confirm graph-navigator still resolves its tools after the frontmatter edit.

stories.title: Give the global workgraph index a regeneration owner and a staleness gate
stories.description: The global workgraph index must be regenerated by a named owner and a check must fail when it trails its sources. Observed 2026-09-22: .prism/shared/workgraph/index.json carries 804 nodes / 778 edges stamped generated 2026-09-12T01:34:09.315Z - 11 days stale. scripts/workgraph-index.mjs exists and is idempotent (its own doctrine is generate, never maintain), but no skill and no sync script re-runs it, so the only multi-root read in the ecosystem silently trails every branch and project change. The index is GENERATED and must never be hand-edited; the fix is an owner plus a gate, not a patched file. New checks named verify-*.mjs under scripts/ are auto-discovered by pre-release-audit.mjs, which puts this on a path already travelled.
steps: Confirm scripts/workgraph-index.mjs regenerates index.json cleanly and is safe to re-run.
Add scripts/verify-workgraph-index.mjs asserting index.json is no more than a set number of days behind the newest source workgraph.
Name the owner that re-runs the generator and record it where the other surface owners are declared.
Regenerate the index once so the stamp is current, and record the resulting node/edge counts.
Verify the gate fails on a deliberately stale stamp and passes after regeneration.

stories.title: Make verify-cards compare the published body it actually read back
stories.description: verify-cards.ps1 must report a card in sync when its published body is byte-identical to the repo file. Observed 2026-09-22 14:11: immediately after DGS v52 and Branch Capture v31 were published and read back byte-identical to the published files, the gate still listed both as stale with missingKB deltas of 46KB and 41KB; four of its six stale rows share the same 4-5KB delta shape (CARDS_OUT_OF_SYNC=8, 84 in sync, 6 stale, 2 no-card). This fix is OBSERVATION-LED: capture the actual injected wrapper from a real published card FIRST, then change the strip to match what the capture shows. A lead to test, explicitly a hypothesis and not the diagnosis: the strip at verify-cards.ps1:44 requires the literal script tag with type="application/json" preceding id="cowork-artifact-meta", so a different attribute order or an extra attribute would leave the wrapper in the hashed body and produce exactly this false stale. Do not edit on that hypothesis alone - confirm it against a captured card first.
steps: Publish or fetch one card and capture its raw published HTML verbatim.
Extract the actual injected meta block, including exact attribute names and order.
Test the current regex at verify-cards.ps1:44 against that captured block and record whether it matches.
Change the strip only to cover what the capture shows; keep hashing the body, never size or mtime.
Re-run the gate against a card whose read-back is byte-identical and confirm it reports in sync.
Confirm no previously in-sync card flips to stale as a result.

stories.title: Resolve codex cards through the registry instead of reporting NO CARD
stories.description: verify-cards.ps1 must resolve a codex to its card through the registry, so a codex that has a live card is never reported as having none. Observed 2026-09-22: the gate listed griot-branch-codex-branch-capture-codex and gbfolio-branch-capture-codex as NO CARD while both had live cards (1Gic4C4XR93Ua538kZzACP and Qucc6tFXG2UDioBm4AddM7); the cause was missing registry rows, not missing cards. Re-verified 2026-09-22 after this pass: both slugs now return 2 matches each in live/dgs-definitive-plan.html, so the registry rows exist and the remaining defect is that the gate does not read them. A gate that reports a present thing as absent trains people to ignore its output, which is the same hole as a gate that cannot fail.
steps: Confirm both codex slugs resolve in the plan registry before changing any logic.
Make verify-cards.ps1 resolve each live/*.html to its card id via the registry rather than by name convention alone.
Keep a genuine missing card reported as NO CARD - the fix narrows a false negative, it must not suppress a true one.
Re-run the gate and confirm zero NO-CARD rows for codexes carrying a registry row.
Confirm a codex with no registry row and no card is still reported.

stories.title: Give the Griot Ontology Codex render an owner and a freshness gate
stories.description: The Griot Ontology Codex render must have a named owner that rebuilds it and a check that fails when it trails the ontology it renders. Observed 2026-09-22: live/griot-ontology-codex.html has mtime 2026-09-11 05:46 while griot-ontology claude/CLAUDE.md is at commit 5e6668b dated 2026-09-22 - 11 days behind, across three doctrine additions it does not show (the skills-save rule, the output style, and the nine tracking systems). propagate.ps1 is the only script in that repo and it syncs copies; it does not render, so no step anywhere rebuilds this page. This is the ungated propagation target class: a copy something writes to and nothing checks. Per the both-halves rule the card republish is part of done, but D6 reserves publishing for the session that runs the dgs-plan-update loop, so this story ends at the repo half plus the gate.
steps: Identify or write the renderer that produces live/griot-ontology-codex.html from claude/CLAUDE.md.
Add the render as a named step in propagate.ps1 so the copy and the render are one action.
Add a check that fails when the rendered codex is older than the ontology last commit.
Regenerate the codex so it carries the three missing doctrine sections.
Verify the gate fails on a deliberately stale render and passes after regeneration.
Record the card republish as a handoff item rather than publishing it in this pass.
